newsitem.title: UK: Disappointed gold loses ground in London PM.
newsitem.headline: Disappointed gold loses ground in London PM.

text.p: Gold slid lower on Monday afternoon as investors skipped out of the market, disappointed by the metal's unimpressive price performance and Wall Street's modest recovery.
The other precious metals also eased in tandem with flagship gold although silver held on to some of its gains from Friday's fund-led rally.
Gold was fixed at $322.60 an ounce in the afternoon compared $326.05 in the morning, shedding the mild gains it had posted on the back of the U.S. stock market's big drop last Friday.
Prices stabilised for the time being around interim support level of $322.50.
But tests of $320 and then $318 could not be ruled out, dealers said.
"(Investors) are very wary of gold. It's been a dreadful investment," said analyst Ted Arnold of Merrill Lynch.
"If they are worried about the stock market falling and want a safe haven they'll go in to cash for a time then maybe bonds, but it's not going to be gold."
Implied gold lease rates have continued to firm after shooting higher last week, which dealers said was a result of producer selling or may even suggest central bank selling.
Dealers said the market would continue watching financial markets for further direction.

The Dow industrials were up some 20 points shortly after the gold fix, after closing down nearly 250 points on Friday. Meanwhile the dollar was firmer against the mark, buoyed by the Dow's solid opening.
The other precious metals came under some pressure with gold, although silver held onto most of the gains it racked up on Friday when several funds covered short positions.
Silver was last indicated at $4.50/$4.52, up six cents from Friday's London close.
Platinum and palladium remain volatile and stumbled slightly in the afternoon along with gold.
Palladium slid some $10 before recovering slightly to a $6.00 weaker $417.00/$420.00, while palladium came off early highs to an unchanged $207.00/$210.00.
"The Russians have been sellers which has been holding the price at bay and keeping the market more liquid," a dealer said.
One-month lease rates were slightly easier with platinum at 10-15 percent and palladium at around 60 percent, he said.
